plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disc. Young flower heads track the sun's movement across the sky, and the plants are widely grown for seeds, oil, and ornamental use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: North America (native), cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, and Asia
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not a single flower but a composite of up to 2,000 tiny individual florets, each of which can develop into a seed.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies. Late-blooming fields in cooler regions are still in flower around this date.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, often lingering into late August at higher elevations
plants.location: Mediterranean region; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years in perfumes, bathing, and cooking, and its name comes from the Latin 'lavare,' meaning 'to wash.'

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower forming dense plumes of tiny golden-yellow flowers atop leafy stems. It colonizes meadows, roadsides, and field edges, providing late-season nectar and pollen for bees, butterflies, and other pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to fall (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Despite popular belief, goldenrod is rarely the cause of hay fever; the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time but has wind-borne pollen.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: An iconic Australian shrub bearing large, striking crimson flower heads surrounded by showy red bracts. Although the main bloom is in spring, in late winter in the Southern Hemisphere the earliest flowers begin to open in warm, sheltered spots in the sandstone forests of the Sydney region.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (August to November) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, especially New South Wales near Sydney and the Blue Mountains
plants.funFact: The waratah is the floral emblem of New South Wales, and its name comes from the Eora Aboriginal word for the plant.
